# Text-to-SQL Models Make Choices Without Saying So

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#specbridge)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.04318v1) · arXiv:2611.04318v1, 3 November 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 22 pages, main sections 1–10, limitations, references, Appendices A–G and all example rows; plotted main results and generator/rewrite figures visually inspected.

## Research question

Executable answers can silently settle consequential calculation choices. Single-reference evaluation cannot distinguish an inability to compute an interpretation from failure to disclose or return an interpretation the model can compute.

## Method

SpecBridge constructs matched open/A-specific/B-specific requests on existing databases, holding other requirements fixed. Executed references distinguish the two interpretations; reviewers and two authors screen the triples. Decide-then-answer enumerates choices before separate generation calls and preserves the original request when adding a user’s choice.

## Evaluation

The main study uses 204 accepted triples across 12 databases, four models, AMBROSIA and selected BIRD cases. Computation uses execution matching; explanation labels use a model judge. The method comparison uses two models and includes a simulated two-turn user.

## What the results support

Among triples where both specific requests are computable, models return both interpretations for only 15–58% of open requests. Deciding first improves coverage over a single-answer baseline; preserving wording reduces losses caused by rewriting unrelated formulas, columns or joins.

## Limits and qualifications

Tests cover one controlled choice and two references, not all interpretations or natural traffic. Open-request outputs outside those references are not penalized; precision is measured on clear requests. Product behavior is reconstructed from documentation, not tested live. User simulation assumes reliable interpretation recognition, and the clause-addition comparison was added after an interim look.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A useful mechanism-focused benchmark for separating SQL capability from disclosure and for testing clarification edits that preserve all other intent constraints.
